question:
A 7-month-old girl is brought to the hospital by her mother, who complains of a lesion on the infant’s labia for the past 5 days. The lesion is 2 x 2 cm in size and red in color with serosanguinous fluid oozing out of the right labia. The parents note that the girl has had a history of recurrent bacterial skin infections with no pus but delayed healing since birth. She also had delayed sloughing of the umbilical cord at birth. Complete blood count results are as follows:
Neutrophils on admission  
Leukocytes 19,000/mm3
Neutrophils 83%
Lymphocytes 10%
Eosinophils 1%
Basophils 1%
Monocytes 5%
Hemoglobin 14 g/dL
Which of the following compounds is most likely to be deficient in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Delayed healing of skin infections and umbilical cord sloughing -> Possible deficiency in cellular adhesion molecule -> 70% CHAIN: Neutrophilia with recurrent bacterial skin infections -> Possible deficiency in integrin subunit -> 60% CHAIN: Neutrophilia with delayed healing -> Possible deficiency in selectin -> 50% CHAIN: Neutrophilia with delayed healing and recurrent infections -> Possible deficiency in vWF -> 40% CHAIN: Neutrophilia with delayed healing and recurrent infections -> Possible deficiency in TNF-alpha -> 70%
enhanced_information: The most likely compound to be deficient in this patient is vWF. The patient's presentation of delayed healing of skin infections and umbilical cord sloughing aligns with a possible deficiency in vWF, supported by the evidence path linking impaired wound healing to von Willebrand Factor.
analysis: The patient's presentation of delayed healing of skin infections and umbilical cord sloughing suggests a possible deficiency in von Willebrand Factor (vWF). This aligns with the enhanced information provided, linking impaired wound healing to vWF deficiency. Given the clinical scenario and the enhanced information, vWF is the most likely compound to be deficient in this patient.
